findings.desc: CHK-004:happy:7 evidence note claims no gemini script in package.json but root package.json line 32 still has test:usage-ledger-codex-gemini pointing to packages/main/dist/tasks/usage-ledger-codex-gemini-smoke.js which does not exist (renamed to usage-ledger-codex-antigravity-smoke.js). The bound command grep -n provider-antigravity||codex-antigravity||provider-gemini||codex-gemini package.json would reveal the stale entry. The file usage-ledger-codex-gemini-smoke.js cannot be found at runtime: node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The intent requires no gemini script in package.json; evidence claim is factually incorrect.

--dangerously-skip-permissions hardcoded in agy argv without story-scope annotation. In runBoundedRealLeafDispatch (line 2003), the antigravity argv includes --dangerously-skip-permissions. This flag is borrowed from the claude-cli.ts path but is not referenced in CHK-001 or the story plan as a confirmed agy CLI flag. If agy does not recognize this flag it receives an unknown argument which may cause unexpected behavior. The path is supervised-only so this is not blocking, but the flag should be annotated with a reference confirming agy supports it.
findings.uncertaintyReason: agy CLI flag support not verified in this review; the flag may be valid for agy or may cause silent failure on unknown flag

findings.desc: prompt text embedded in argv array for agy dispatch creates a large argvDigest payload. In runBoundedRealLeafDispatch for hostKind=antigravity, the full prompt file content (promptText) is passed as the --print argument inside the argv array. The argvDigest = sha256(JSON(argv)) digests the entire array including the prompt. This is I/O-isolation-correct (no raw content returned in result) but the argv digest string in ProviderExecResult will be a hash of a potentially large payload. This is consistent with the existing design and not a blocker; noting as an informational edge case for reviewers.
